steps.content: The idea says a coin trading near its recent high is strong and keeps rising, so the factor should rise when the close sits near the recent high. The simplest form is the share of the recent high that the close occupies, which is unit-free and comparable across coins. I'll test that first.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0476
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0210 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0277, 2023 +0.0195, 2024 +0.0191

The simple form already works well: incremental IC +0.0210 with t = 8.7 and the same sign in all three sub-periods. Since the idea stresses "near its recent high" rather than the absolute level, I'll try a shorter 3-day window to see whether a fresher recent high sharpens the effect.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0443
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0194 (t = 7.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0264, 2023 +0.0177, 2024 +0.0174

The 3-day window is clearly worse (+0.0194 vs +0.0210), so the effect of the recent high is a slower, persistent one, not a fresh one. I'll stop there and keep the 5-day version, which is also the more stable of the two.

The idea says coins trading more per dollar (price per dollar) earn higher returns, so the factor should rise with the per-unit-volume return. I'll start with the simplest form: the average daily return divided by average daily USDT volume over a 10-day window.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0185
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0046 (t = -3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0080, 2023 -0.0012, 2024 -0.0063

The 10-day average per-unit-volume return is negative in every sub-period (−0.0046, t = −3.3), so on this history illiquid coins did worse. I'll try a shorter 5-day window to see whether the direction is consistent across window lengths.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0182
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0043 (t = -2.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0076, 2023 +0.0001, 2024 -0.0069

The 5-day window is also negative (−0.0043) and less consistent across periods. Since the direction is negative in both short and long windows, I'll stop testing and hand in the best-tested version.

What I found: the idea does not hold on this history. Coins whose price moves more per dollar traded (average daily return per dollar of volume) went on to underperform, with incremental IC around −0.005 (t ≈ −3) in all sub-periods, so the effect is not a window artifact. I keep the direction the idea states rather than flipping it to chase the score.

<factor>(Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=1)) - 1).safe_div(Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=10, min_periods=8))</factor>

The idea says heavy aggressive buying exhausts demand and the price falls back, so the factor should go down when aggressive buying is high. I'll start with the simplest reading: the recent average taker buy share, negated, since that's the quantity the idea names.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0034
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0090 (t = -3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0194, 2023 -0.0053, 2024 -0.0074

The simple version came out negative (−0.0090, consistent across all three sub-periods), so heavy aggressive buying did not predict weakness on this history. Since the idea talks about "heavy" buying, I'll check whether a sharper, shorter window (3 days) behaves differently, keeping the same direction.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0040
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0085 (t = -2.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0194, 2023 -0.0043, 2024 -0.0072

The 3-day window gave −0.0085, essentially the same as the 5-day version (−0.0090), so the window length isn't the issue. I'll stop here rather than keep re-testing on the same history.

What I found: the idea does not hold on this data. The recent average taker buy share, negated, has a rank IC of +0.0034 (so the raw quantity points mildly the way the idea says), but once liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum are removed it is −0.0090 with t = −3.0, and negative in every sub-period (2022H2 −0.0194, 2023 −0.0053, 2024 −0.0074). That means heavy aggressive buying on this sample went with *better* subsequent returns, not weaker. I keep the direction the idea states and submit the simplest form, which was the best of the ones I tried.

<factor>-1 * Factor('taker_quote_vol').safe_div(Factor('quote_volume')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about average trade count per day, and it says more trades per day is bullish, so the factor is the daily trade count averaged over a window, with no sign flip. I'll start with the simplest form: 20-day mean of `num_trades`.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0402
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0025 (t = -2.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0013, 2023 -0.0033, 2024 -0.0024

The plain 20-day mean gives incremental IC −0.0025 with the same sign in all three sub-periods, so on this history average trade count is mildly bearish. Since the idea says "many trades per day" rather than "many trades in total", I'll test the average trade count per day directly, which is a different quantity from the raw 20-day sum.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0204
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0134 (t = -4.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0248, 2023 -0.0143, 2024 -0.0067

The per-day ratio is clearly worse (−0.0134, and negative in every sub-period), so the raw average trade count per day is the better form. I'll stop here rather than keep hunting on this history.

What I found: the idea points the wrong way on this data. Coins with more trades per day did slightly *worse* over the next days (rank IC −0.040, incremental −0.0025, negative in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024), and the per-day ratio version was worse still, so I keep the direction the idea states and submit the simple 20-day average of trade count.

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0194, 2023 -0.0053, 2024 -0.0074

Before concluding, I'll check whether a longer window (10 days) behaves differently, since the idea speaks of "heavy aggressive buying" as a sustained event rather than a recent one.

What I found: the idea points the wrong way on this data. The negative of the 5-day average taker buy share had incremental IC −0.0090 with t = −3.0 and the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, so on July 2022–December 2024 heavy aggressive buying has been followed by *better* returns, not a back-down. I'm keeping the direction the idea states (minus heavy taker buying), but I report honestly that it does not work on this history.

The idea says more trades per day → better forward returns, so the factor should rise with the average number of trades per day. Since trade count is already comparable across coins (it's a count, not a price), I'll start with the simplest form: a 20-day mean of `num_trades`.

rank IC: -0.0402
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0025 (t = -2.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0013, 2023 -0.0033, 2024 -0.0024

The raw 20-day average of trade count comes out at −0.04 rank IC and −0.0025 incremental, consistently negative in all three sub-periods — on this history, more trades per day has actually been worse. Before concluding, I'll check whether the effect is an artifact of a few unusually high-trade-day coins by using a median instead of a mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0315
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 0.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0007, 2023 -0.0003, 2024 +0.0000

The median is essentially flat (+0.0000, t = 0.0) and its sub-periods flip sign, so it doesn't improve on the mean. Since the idea is specifically about *many trades per day*, I'll try emphasizing those days with a square — squaring the daily trade count weights heavy-trade days much more than light ones, which is a different way to say "many trades per day".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0204

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0248, 2023 -0.0143, 2024 -0.0067

What I found: on this history the idea does not hold — coins with many trades per day went on to underperform, and the effect is not an outlier-driven artifact (the median version is flat, the squared version is negative and consistent across sub-periods). I keep the direction the idea states and submit the 20-day average of `num_trades` as the factor.

The average taker buy share is positively related to next-day returns — heavy aggressive buying has been followed by *better* returns, not by exhaustion — and the incremental IC is negative in every sub-period (2022H2 −0.0194, 2023 −0.0053, 2024 −0.0074) with t = −3.0. I kept the direction the idea states rather than flipping it to chase the sign, so the factor below is the one I tested and found to be wrong on this history.

<factor>-1 * Factor('taker_quote_vol').safe_div(Factor('quote_volume')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea says price moves *more per dollar traded* — that is, the average daily return divided by average dollar volume, i.e. a liquidity-adjusted return. Since the idea says illiquidity is *bullish*, the factor is the ratio itself, not its negative. I'll start with the simplest form: 5-day mean return divided by 5-day mean USDT volume.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0214
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0004 (t = 0.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0049, 2023 +0.0028, 2024 +0.0007

The plain 5-day version is essentially flat (incremental +0.0004, t = 0.3) and flips sign in 2022H2. Since the ratio is noisy day to day, I'll smooth it over a few days to see whether the effect is just a slow, noisy property of the measure.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0248
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0063 (t = -3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0099, 2023 -0.0077, 2024 -0.0031

Smoothing made it worse (−0.0063, consistent across all three sub-periods), so the effect is not an artifact of noise. That is two tests in a row without improving on the best, so I'll stop and report honestly.

What I found: the idea does not hold on this history. The plain 5-day liquidity-adjusted return is essentially flat (+0.0004 incremental, t = 0.3) and its raw rank IC is −0.02, meaning coins with large average daily returns per dollar traded actually did *worse* over the next days, not better. Smoothing the same ratio further made it clearly negative (−0.0063, t = −3.0, negative in every sub-period), so the effect is not a slow, noisy property of the measure. I keep the direction the idea states rather than flipping it to chase the score.

Aggressive selling is measured as the taker share of quote volume (taker_quote_vol / quote_volume), which is comparable across coins regardless of price or volume scale. I'll start with the simplest version: minus the 5-day average of the taker share.

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0194, 2023 -0.0053, 2024 -0.0074

What I found: the negative of recent aggressive selling (taker share of quote volume) has a small positive raw rank IC (+0.0034) but a strongly negative incremental IC (−0.0090, t = −3.0) in every sub-period, so on 2022-07 to 2024-12 aggressive selling was followed by underperformance, not a bounce — the direction the idea asks for is not supported. The 10-day version was weaker still, so I hand in the 5-day form.

I'll start with the simplest form: minus the 20-day average of daily return divided by average daily volume, using USDT volume so it's comparable across coins.
